question: On the Stage A harder Burgers pilot, with the Stage D sensors32_bursts mask, does the Fourier neural operator still have lower hard_ood mean relative viscosity error than a weak-form identifier and a solver-in-the-loop fit? A negative answer is an acceptable outcome.
estimator_notes: Weak form: Burgers is known. Nu is the only unknown. Each test function is separable, phi(x, t) = psi(x) eta(t), with psi and eta equal to (1 - xi^2)_+^degree. Derivatives fall on phi. The field is never differentiated. Integrals use the periodic trapezoidal rule on the sensor nodes and the trapezoidal rule in time, with half-weights on the first and last frame of each burst. Bursts are pooled into one normal equation. There is no interpolation of u. Solver, sensor lift: The initial condition is the real-FFT zero-pad lift of the 32 (or fewer) sensors at frame 0 onto the N=1024 grid, the same lift_sensors map as Stage D. Modes above the sensor Nyquist are zero. This is interpolation, and it is not a Burgers state. The fit then matches the true spectral solver to the sensors on the later bursts. It does not read off-sensor samples. Solver, oracle initial condition: The initial condition is the stored full-grid field at frame 0. The fit matches the true spectral solver to the same later-burst sensors. This ceiling reads the initial condition off the sensors. It is not a sparse-sensor estimator.

timing.notes: Solver times are wall-clock seconds per test instance for the full coarse-grid plus golden-section search, including every forward solve, on this CPU with the worker count in the protocol. The FNO time is one instance of the same 191-point rollout the Stage D inverse evaluates. The network is the Stage D architecture with random initial weights, because the published checkpoints are not in the repository. The arithmetic does not depend on those weights. Closed-form time was not the object of the measurement and is stored as 0.

fno_stage_d_grid.weights: randomly initialized Stage D architecture; not a published checkpoint

stress.notes: Weak form is scored on the full Stage E condition list at noise seed 0. The solver-in-the-loop stress is only the sensor-lift initial condition, only hard_ood, and only the four Stage E cells where the published operator mean relative error crossed 10% or the sensor count dropped. A full solver grid was outside the CPU budget. Published Stage E aggregates in the comparison columns are read from docs/v02/stage_e_scores.json by this script. They are not a new operator run. The one-burst mask has no solver target and is not in the solver list. Noise is the Stage E full-field Gaussian model. After the noisy field is built, each estimator reads only its mask.

advantage.paragraph: On hard_ood, the published comparison is the FNO against closed-form residual least squares (0.3494591802034973, 9 failures). The data-only FNO mean relative error (0.04948720846902754) is lower error than the weak form (0.08978429715170869). The data-only FNO mean relative error (0.04948720846902754) is higher error than the sensor-lift solver (0.01379664899082717). The data-only FNO mean relative error (0.04948720846902754) is higher error than the oracle-IC solver (0.002512684392086404). The hybrid 1e-2 FNO mean relative error (0.03368266375533967) is lower error than the weak form (0.08978429715170869). The hybrid 1e-2 FNO mean relative error (0.03368266375533967) is higher error than the sensor-lift solver (0.01379664899082717). The hybrid 1e-2 FNO mean relative error (0.03368266375533967) is higher error than the oracle-IC solver (0.002512684392086404). The advantage over the closed form does not survive as a claim that the operator beats a weak-form identifier and a solver-in-the-loop fit. At least one of those baselines has hard_ood mean relative error at or below an FNO arm. The oracle initial-condition solver is a ceiling that sees the full field at t = 0. It is not evidence about a sensor-only method.

limitations: One scalar viscosity, one-dimensional periodic Burgers, and the Stage A pilot. This is not a multi-equation benchmark.
The weak form never interpolates u. With five frames in a burst the time integral is a five-node trapezoidal rule. Degree, radius, and center stride were fixed before test scoring and were not swept.
The sensor-lift solver interpolates frame 0 only. The Stage D operator also sees frames 1 through 4. Both match the later bursts and not the opening burst.
The oracle initial-condition solver reads the full field at t = 0. It is a ceiling, not a sensor-only method.

The solver search is a 7-point coarse grid plus at most 10 golden-section steps, down to a bracket of width 0.0005. It is not an exhaustive 191-point grid. A missed local minimum would be a property of that search.
Fourier neural operator errors are the committed Stage D per-instance estimates at lambda 0. Those networks were not retrained in this run, and the published checkpoints are not in the repository.

The Fourier neural operator wall clock is one instance of the Stage D 191-point rollout with a randomly initialized network of the Stage D architecture. It measures the arithmetic, not a published checkpoint.
Solver stress covers four Stage E cells on hard_ood only. The weak form covers the full Stage E condition list at noise seed 0.
Stage E noise is scaled by the clean full-field standard deviation. The estimators then read the mask. They do not read the clean field.
